ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In $\odot O$, $\overline{EC}$ and $\overline{AB}$ are diameters, and $\angle BOD \cong \angle DOE \cong \angle EOF \cong \angle FOA$. Find $m\widehat{EB}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with O as the center, and A, B, C, D, E, F are on the circle. Segment AB passes through the center O and is a diameter; segment EC also passes through the center O and is a diameter. Along the upper-left semicircle direction from A to B, the order of the points is A, F, E, D, B, so minor arc EB is composed of arc ED and arc DB. Reasoning: Because AB is a diameter, the central angle corresponding to this semicircle side from ray OA to ray OB is 180°. The problem gives that ∠BOD, ∠DOE, ∠EOF, ∠FOA are congruent; they exactly divide this semicircle into 4 equal central angles, so each angle is 180° ÷ 4 = 45°. The central angle corresponding to arc EB equals ∠EOD + ∠DOB, that is 45° + 45° = 90°. Therefore m arc EB = 90.

raw_record.question_text: In $\odot O$, $\overline{EC}$ and $\overline{AB}$ are diameters, and $\angle BOD \cong \angle DOE \cong \angle EOF \cong \angle FOA$. Find $m\widehat{EB}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: around the upper-left to upper-right part of the circle the points occur in the order E, D, B, so the minor arc EB is made of arcs ED and DB. The rays OA, OF, OE, OD, and OB partition the semicircle from A to B. From the text, AB is a diameter, so the central angle from OA to OB along that side is 180 degrees. The text also states that angles BOD, DOE, EOF, and FOA are congruent; these are the four adjacent central angles filling that semicircle. Therefore each is 180/4 = 45 degrees. Arc EB equals arc ED plus arc DB, corresponding to central angles DOE and BOD, so m arc EB = 45 + 45 = 90.
